_comment: S4 (spec-v2/03-selection.md) / Wave 5.8. `modules` is the protected set the basename-contains-selection matcher cannot see (focus, offsetDomain, caretPositions, v1 backend/IME offenders). Basename `selection` is a fail-closed net so selectionReader.ts cannot silently escape. `outOfScope` is a decision that a file is not a selection module — not a waiver. `entries` waive a live timer in an in-scope file; each needs file, enclosing symbol, kind, and a reason that names why the site remains and which wave retires it. Remove an entry in the same PR that deletes the call. Liveness checks the named symbol and kind, not merely the path.

outOfScope.reason: Not a Wave 5.8 selection module. scheduleFlush coalesces commit/decoration DOM reconcile onto the next animation frame — a Wave 03 DomScheduler stand-in (SCH), not a selection retry. projectSelection is a post-flush callback, not the reason for the timer. S4 does not apply; listing it here is the decision, not an allowlist waiver.

entries.reason: Wave 05 replaces this with the selection engine's own write window. This is NOT a projection retry - the two projector retries this list used to hold were deleted when the Firefox authority-range fix landed, because a rAF there was a missing attach in disguise. This one is the backends' self-echo suppression window: applySelectionUntilNextFrame raises applyingSelectionDepth and drops it a frame later so a backend's own selection write is not read back as a user gesture, and it has nine callers across contenteditableBackendCore, editContextBackendCore, editContextBackendSelection and expandedContentEditableBackend. Removing it means giving the backends a synchronous end-of-write signal, which is Wave 05's job. FIELD-EDITOR-TEARDOWN.md also records it as an uncancelled leftover on reset().

Wave 05 retires this when the selection engine owns DOM-match after decoration changes. UNINVESTIGATED WAIVER recorded the moment isSelectionModule widened from a selection* prefix to a basename that contains selection: this file is a selection module by any reading of S4 and the prefix matcher walked past it. The shape is a deferred ensureActiveDOMMatchesYText plus restoreDOMSelectionFromEditor — treat the rAF as a missing attach or a wrong seam, not an engine accommodation. Whoever takes Wave 05's backend write window owns deleting it; do not renew without saying what the next frame observes that this turn cannot.

Wave 05 retires this by activating the post-destructure caret in the same turn as the replace. UNINVESTIGATED WAIVER from the isSelectionModule widen: a React primitive whose basename contains Selection, walked past by the prefix matcher. The shape is activateTextSelection plus focus deferred one frame after replaceInlineAtomWithText — S4's missing-attach class. Wave 05 owns the delete.

Wave 03 retires this by routing the toolbar rect through the scheduler read phase. UNINVESTIGATED WAIVER from the isSelectionModule widen. The shape is a measurement retry: update() cancels the previous frame and schedules resolveNativeSelectionRect on the next — the same class as the selectionRect rAF that another agent deleted today. Wave 03 overlay work owns the delete; do not renew without saying what the second measurement observes that the first cannot.

Wave 05 step 5.5 retires this when §5.3 mount ack makes attach same-flush and §5.4 rewrites focusController. waitForAttachment polls `_getAttachedElement()?.isConnected` (and matching blockId) for up to four frames; this entry is the retry inside waiter.check (`requestAnimationFrame(waiter.check)`). The thing it is waiting for is a mount ack, not a browser caret settle — the same missing-attach class that already made two projector rAFs unnecessary once attach ran in-turn. resolveAttachmentWaiters can complete a waiter early; after 5.5 the initial check should be enough.

Wave 05 step 5.5 retires this with the sibling retry above. This entry is the initial `requestAnimationFrame(check)` that starts the waiter. Same wait: the focused block's attached element is not connected in this turn. §5.3 parks a projection on the missing element and the ack projects in the same flush's write phase, so a frame poll of isConnected has nothing left to observe.

Wave 05 step 5.5 mount ack retires this. trySyncBackend waits up to three frames for resolveCellInlineElement to return a mounted cell host, then attachElement + placeCaretInCell (a native selection write). The wait is a missing cell-host attach, not a selection-engine accommodation. In scope because the success path writes window.getSelection(); Wave 5.8's 'may survive as non-selection' does not hold for a file whose job on success is a caret write. After 5.5 the cell host is acked same-flush and the retry has nothing left to wait for.

Wave 05 step 5.6 / §8 C3 retires this. Safari may fire compositionend before the final DOM mutation; the rAF waits one frame for that mutation before reconcileAfterComposition. C3 replaces this with input-event sequence tracking (composition event sequence on contenteditable; EditContext textupdate ordering on Chromium) so reconcile runs after the backend observes DOM quiescence in the same task-queue turn. No setTimeout-based composition timer is permitted; the 50ms GBoard path above this call is a Date.now() comparison, not a timer, and dies with the same rewrite.
